newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech leader takes surprise trip to Italy, Holland.
newsitem.headline: Czech leader takes surprise trip to Italy, Holland.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel and his wife Dagmar left unexpectedly on Friday for an 18-day "recuperation" trip to the Italian Alps and the Netherlands, Havel's spokesman said in a statement.

Havel, who has been recovering from surgery which removed a small cancerous tumour along with half of a lung last December, is to receive regular visits from a doctor during the trip, spokesman Ladislav Spacek said.
The specific destinations or further details of the trip were not disclosed.
Havel, 60, returned to his regular presidential duties last month, hosting two state visits including Norway's King Harald in March and French President Jacques Chirac, who left Prague on Thursday.

The former chain-smoking dissident playwright who led the bloodless 1989 "Velvet Revolution" over communism told Czech Television this week that he would "soon" decide whether to seek another five-year term in 1998.
The Czech president is not elected directly but by obtaining a three-fifths majority in parliament. Havel was elected to his current term after the split of Czechoslovakia at the beginning of 1993.
Opinion polls show Havel, whose duties are more ceremonial than political, has maintained the broad popularity which brought him to power after the revolution.

The president and his new wife, the former actress Dagmar Veskrnova who is now known in the Czech feminine as Havlova, made a similar surprise trip in February to Spa in Belgium, with no prior public announcement.
Doctors have said that his recovery has progressed without complications and required no further "radical" treatment.
Havel surprised his fellow citizens when he married in a small secret ceremony at a Prague district town hall on January 4 soon after his release from hospital.
The new first lady, 44, is well known to Czechs for leading roles in numerous films, television programmes, and plays.
Havel's first wife Olga died of cancer, aged 62, in January, 1996.
